When our employees bring their best and succeed, the Company succeeds.

About the Role

The Actuarial Analyst III is an experienced actuarial professional responsible for performing advanced actuarial analyses, forecasting, financial modeling, pricing, and reporting activities that support key business decisions across the organization. This role applies actuarial principles and statistical techniques to evaluate financial performance, analyze healthcare utilization trends, develop pricing recommendations, and support strategic initiatives.

The Actuarial Analyst III serves as a subject matter resource within the department, working independently on complex assignments while collaborating with actuarial leadership and business partners to deliver data-driven insights that support organizational goals.

What You'll Do

Data Analysis & Reporting

  • Collect, analyze, and interpret financial, claims, membership, and utilization data to support actuarial studies and business initiatives.

  • Develop and maintain recurring actuarial reports, dashboards, and analyses.

  • Support the monitoring and reporting of key financial and operational metrics, including Incurred But Not Reported (IBNR) estimates.

  • Validate data integrity and ensure accuracy of actuarial analyses and reporting.

Trend Analysis & Forecasting

  • Perform trend analyses to evaluate healthcare cost, utilization, and membership patterns.

  • Support forecasting activities related to medical costs, enrollment, utilization, and financial performance.

  • Analyze historical data and emerging trends to assist in projecting future business outcomes.

  • Identify opportunities and risks through quantitative analysis and predictive modeling.

Pricing & Financial Analysis

  • Develop, maintain, and enhance actuarial pricing models.

  • Support product pricing and financial evaluations, including:

  • Rate development and regulatory filings

  • Benefit adjustment factor analysis

  • Fee schedule evaluations

  • New product pricing

  • Cost and profitability analyses

  • Assist in assessing the financial impact of benefit, provider, and regulatory changes.

  • Provide analytical support for strategic business initiatives and product development efforts.

Professional Development & Collaboration

  • Apply actuarial principles and methodologies to solve complex business challenges.

  • Collaborate with Finance, Underwriting, Product Development, Operations, and other business teams.

  • Present analytical findings and recommendations to actuarial leadership and business stakeholders.

  • Support process improvement initiatives designed to enhance efficiency, reporting accuracy, and analytical capabilities.

  • Continue professional actuarial development through exam progression and technical skill enhancement.

Education/Experience:

  • Bachelor degree is required preferably within Mathematics, Statistics, Actuarial Sciences or a related field from an accredited college or university.

Additional licensing, certifications, registrations:

  • ASA candidate a plus.


Knowledge:

  • Requires expert knowledge of Excel.

  • Prefers working knowledge of Access or other database application.

  • Prefers experience with SAS or other programming language.

  • Requires knowledge of data analysis and Actuarial principles.


Skills and Abilities:

  • Requires good oral and written communication skills.

  • Requires strong analytical thinking.

  • Requires strong mathematical skill and statistical analysis abilities.

  • Requires good judgment and problem solving skills.

At Horizon, you’ll do meaningful work that directly improves lives—while being supported by a mission‑driven organization that values expertise, collaboration, and growth. We believe that when our people thrive, our communities do too. If you are passionate about making an impact, we’d love to hear from you!

  • Conduct MST assessment including review of referral information, identifying, and engaging key participants, identifying systemic strengths and weaknesses, and developing an analysis of the fit of problem behaviors within the ecological context. Maintains a caseload of 4-6 families.
  • Engage primary caregiver(s) and other key participants in active change-oriented treatment by identifying and overcoming barriers to engagement.
  • Implement a problem conceptualization, treatment planning, intervention implementation, outcomes review and strategy revision procedure using the MST Analytic Process.
  • Maintain clear and concise documentation of treatment efforts that promote peer and supervisory review and feedback, and that demonstrate compliance with the nine MST Principles and the MST Analytic Process.
  • Ability to engage and collaborate with all relevant systems and key participants within each system, to maintain alignment throughout MST treatment.
  • Provide direct clinical treatment using methods compatible with MST principles and practices.
  • Participate in all MST training, weekly supervision, consultation, and MST Therapist development activities.
  • All services are provided in a person centered, trauma informed manner.

Sign-On-Bonus: $2,000 payable at the 6-month mark, contingent upon: all required training completed, no personnel actions, and performance metrics met.

Position Summary:

The CCTV Operator is responsible for operating and monitoring surveillance systems to safeguard people, property, and infrastructure at client locations across South India. This role involves real-time monitoring, incident detection, reporting, and supporting emergency response through CCTV systems, access control integration, and event logging.

Key Responsibilities:

1. CCTV Surveillance Monitoring:

  • Monitor multiple live camera feeds in real-time from control rooms across various zones.
  • Ensure continuous surveillance of critical and sensitive zones such as entry/exit points, lobbies, warehouses, data centers, etc.
  • Immediately alert on-site security supervisors in case of suspicious activity, safety violations, or emergencies.

2. Incident Management:

  • Respond swiftly to unusual or abnormal activity, including intrusion, fire alarms, loitering, or unauthorized access.
  • Maintain video evidence and submit incident clips to relevant teams following chain-of-custody protocols.
  • Assist site teams during live incidents by guiding them using visual monitoring.

3. Access Control Support:

  • Monitor and verify access control events if CCTV is integrated with turnstiles, boom barriers, or biometric systems.
  • Cross-check identity and authorization of personnel or vehicles as per client SOPs.
  • Flag tailgating, force entries, or violation of visitor movement policy.

4. Video Archiving & Retrieval:

  • Ensure timely recording and safe storage of CCTV footage as per the site’s retention policy.
  • Retrieve historical footage upon request from the client or internal G4S supervisors.
  • Maintain accurate logbooks of footage access and storage transfers.

5. Equipment Maintenance Support:

  • Conduct regular checks on all CCTV equipment including cameras, DVR/NVRs, monitors, switches, and power backups.
  • Coordinate with the technical support team or client vendor for maintenance, servicing, or repairs.
  • Report any malfunctioning cameras or broken connections immediately.

6. Reporting & Documentation:

  • Maintain daily control room logs, shift handover notes, and incident records.
  • Submit daily/weekly security reports including observations, alerts raised, and footage reviewed.
  • Follow confidentiality protocols and restrict sharing of sensitive visual data.

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Education: Minimum 12th Pass. Diploma in Electronics, IT, or Computer Applications preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 1–3 years of experience in CCTV operation/control room roles
    • Experience in malls, tech parks, industrial plants, hospitals, or logistics hubs preferred
  • Age: 21–45 years
  • Language Proficiency: Working knowledge of English + regional language (Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam) is mandatory based on location.
  • Typing & Computer Skills: Basic computer operation skills required (MS Word, Excel, CCTV software usage)

Key Skills & Competencies:

  • Alertness and high situational awareness
  • Familiarity with analog/IP cameras, DVRs/NVRs, VMS platforms
  • Calmness under pressure and strong incident judgment
  • Team coordination and communication
  • Ethical conduct, confidentiality, and integrity
  • Ability to work in 12-hour rotational shifts (day/night)

Work Conditions:

  • 8–12 hour shifts, rotating day/night schedules
  • Indoor, air-conditioned control room environment
  • Uniform and ID card will be issued as per client or site requirements
  • May be required to work on holidays/weekends depending on duty roster

Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary in line with Minimum Wages (Skilled category) for the state – Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala
  • ESI, PF, Bonus, Gratuity, and Leave benefits as per statutory compliance

title: Medical Record Unit Examiner I/II/III (Claims)
description:
Job Description:

Summary:

Responsible for managing and providing divisional support to all Medical Records Unit (MRU) activities such as medical record requests, receipts, research and tracking through the medical record database. Research Facets, Plan Connexion processing system and control workflow to ensure intakes are handled timely by the appropriate area, including BlueCard and Local claims, to ensure performance metrics are met.


Essential Accountabilities:

Level I

• Responsible for the quality assurance of all internal and external medical record requests and the determination of appropriate outgoing communication.

• Review medical record receipts including unsolicited medical records for completeness and determine appropriate workflow.

• Interface with and extract data from the Facets and/or Plan Connexion processing systems to prepare and complete medical record reports.

• Process and maintain current and accurate Department of Labor medical record requests.

• Assist Claim Examiners with questions.

• Initiate and participate in learning opportunities around regulations, systems, procedures and skills needed for the role.

• Consistently demonstrates high standards of integrity by supporting the Lifetime Healthcare Companies’ mission and values, adhering to the Corporate Code of Conduct, and leading to the Lifetime Way values and beliefs.

• Maintains high regard for member privacy in accordance with the corporate privacy policies and procedures.

• Regular and reliable attendance is expected and required.

• Performs other functions as assigned by management.


Level II (in addition to Level I Accountabilities)

• Efficiently resolve escalated organizational requests and inquiries.

• Identify trends, determine root cause and recommend potential solution.

• Research, track and resolve Department of Labor medical record requests for Home plan including Plan Connexion.

• Resolve all types of medical record review transactions which includes Host and Local claims.

• Observe fluctuations in inventory levels and escalate to Level III for investigation.

• Train Level I employees on department processes/functions.


Level III (in addition to Level II Accountabilities)

• Resolve medical record review transactions which includes Host, Home and Local claims.

• Identify trends, determine root cause, communicate risk to leadership and initiate action for resolution.

• Mentor and train on lines of business within MRU.

• Support analytical work.

• Serve as subject matter expert testing new system implementations and improvements.

• Identify, recommend and initiate process as well as desk level documentation improvements.

• Provide productional support to areas outside of MRU based on business need.

• Participate as subject matter expert in project and process improvement related work for MRU.

• Responsible for maintenance of the Medical Record Database.

• Monitoring inventory fluctuations within workstreams to coordinate, delegate and execute inventory control/assignment plan.

• Coordinate invoicing for payment of medical records.

• Learn and support areas outside of MRU.

• Provide resolution of complex and escalated issues.


Minimum Qualifications:


NOTE:

We include multiple levels of classification differentiated by demonstrated knowledge, skills, and the ability to manage increasingly independent and/or complex assignments, broader responsibility, additional decision making, and in some cases, becoming a resource to others. In addition to using this differentiated approach to place new hires, it also provides guideposts for employee development and promotional opportunities.


All Levels

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Office experience and claims background preferred.

• Basic computer skills required including the ability to navigate in a Windows environment. Able to work between multiple programs and applications at the same time.

• Strong self-management skills including but not limited to reasoning, problem-solving, change management, communication, time management and organizational skills.

• Ability to meet minimum performance metrics.

• Ability to arrive on time at work and as scheduled.


Level II (in addition to Level I Qualifications)

• Ability to analyst data and identify trends.

• Ability to mentor and train.

• Exceed performance expectations for a minimum of one (1) year and/or meet performance expectations for three (3) years as a Level I.


Level III (in addition to Level I Qualifications)

• Demonstrated in-depth knowledge of, and ability to coach/support MRU on all lines of business and other areas within Claims.

• Exceed performance expectations for a minimum of three (3) years and/or meet performance expectations for five (5) years.


Physical Requirements:

• The ability to hear, understand, and speak clearly while using a phone, with or without a headset.

• Ability to work while sitting and/or standing at a workstation viewing a computer and using a keyboard, mouse and/or phone for three (3) or more hours at a time.

• Ability to travel across the Health Plan service region for meetings and/or trainings as needed.


************


In support of the Americans with Disabilities Act, this job description lists only those responsibilities and qualifications deemed essential to the position.


Equal Opportunity Employer

This position is for an Electrical and Instrumentation (E&I) Technician located in Martinsville, IL. title: FLIGHT SOFTWARE SYSTEMS ENGINEER
location: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center - Greenbelt, MD 20771
description:
JOB SUMMARY: The NASA Software Engineering Services III (SES-III) contract provides engineering expertise supporting the development, integration, testing, deployment, and sustainment of NASA flight software systems. MVS is seeking a Flight Software Systems Engineer (Chief) to provide end-to-end flight software systems engineering leadership supporting the Advanced Limb Infrared Chemistry Experiment (ALICE) instrument for NASA's Stratosphere-Troposphere Research via Innovative Viewing Experiments (STRIVE) mission at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) in Greenbelt, Maryland.

STRIVE is NASA's next-generation Earth Science mission designed to improve understanding of atmospheric processes, including stratosphere-troposphere interactions and their impact on ozone, weather, climate, and air quality. The ALICE instrument provides advanced infrared limb observations of atmospheric temperature, ozone, trace gases, aerosols, and clouds with unprecedented spatial resolution and sensitivity.

The Flight Software Systems Engineer serves as the technical authority responsible for the complete software systems engineering lifecycle supporting the ALICE instrument. This position provides leadership from mission formulation through mission operations, including conceptual design, software requirements engineering, architecture development, interface definition, implementation oversight, integration, verification and validation, launch preparation, and on-orbit sustainment. The successful candidate will collaborate across multidisciplinary engineering teams while remaining technically engaged in software architecture, embedded flight software development, and system integration activities. Work Schedule: This is a part-time position. Location: Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC), Greenbelt, MD. This position is hybrid.

PRIMARY DUTIES

  • Lead end-to-end Flight Software Systems Engineering activities throughout the complete mission lifecycle.

  • Develop and maintain flight software concepts of operation, system architecture, software requirements, interface definitions, and technical baselines.

  • Analyze mission, spacecraft, and instrument requirements and decompose them into detailed software system and subsystem requirements.

  • Lead software architecture development, software allocation, interface design, and technical solution development supporting the ALICE instrument.

  • Develop program specifications, Interface Control Documents (ICDs), Requirements Verification Matrices (RVMs), and software verification plans.

  • Participate in software implementation activities including coding, integration, debugging, and technical oversight of embedded flight software developed primarily in C/C++.

  • Develop and maintain system test procedures supporting unit, integration, system, environmental, and mission-level testing.

  • Coordinate software development activities across systems engineering, flight software, hardware, avionics, instrument engineering, integration & test, cybersecurity, and mission operations teams.

  • Lead software technical reviews including SRR, PDR, CDR, TRR, FRR, and peer reviews.

  • Identify technical risks, perform engineering trade studies, and develop mitigation strategies.

  • Support observatory integration, environmental testing, launch preparation, early orbit operations, and mission sustainment.

  • Mentor software and systems engineers while serving as a Chief Technologist or Core Group Lead.

REQUIREMENTS

  • Experience leading software systems engineering across concept development, requirements, architecture, implementation, integration, verification, validation, deployment, and maintenance.

  • Experience developing software architectures, program specifications, interface definitions, and verification strategies.

  • Experience developing embedded flight software using C/C++, Python, Java, FORTRAN, or similar languages.

  • Experience analyzing, designing, programming, testing, debugging, and maintaining secure mission-critical software.

  • Experience translating mission and system requirements into detailed software designs and implementation plans.

  • Experience integrating flight software with spacecraft avionics, scientific instruments, and ground systems.

  • Experience using Git, GitLab, or equivalent configuration management systems.

  • Excellent leadership, communication, and technical writing skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • NASA Flight Software Systems Engineering experience.

  • Earth Science mission experience.

  • Instrument Flight Software development.

  • Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) and SysML.

  • DOORS, Jama, or equivalent requirements management tools.

  • RTEMS, VxWorks, or embedded Linux.

  • CCSDS protocols, SpaceWire, and spacecraft communication interfaces.

  • CI/CD pipelines and automated software verification.

  • Participation in SRR, PDR, CDR, SIR, TRR, FRR, ORR, and Launch Readiness Reviews.

  • Launch and on-orbit mission operations support.

RELEVANT EXPERIENCE: 20+ years of experience in software systems engineering supporting aerospace, spacecraft, or embedded real-time software systems.

EDUCATION/CERTIFICATION: Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or a related technical discipline.

SECURITY CLEARANCE: Must be a U.S. Citizen and eligible to obtain the required National Agency Check (NAC) clearance.

title: Project Lead – H4D Problem Curation
description:
About the Role:

At BMNT, Project Leads play an integral role in our consulting practice. Their goal is to independently lead aspects of the program and achieve the results a customer wants related to specific projects and/or lines of effort. They strategize with, and provide overall support to, Program Managers (PM) on day-to-day customer operations and contract management. This is the introductory project level in BMNT’s Program Leadership track.

As the Project Lead I for the H4D (Hacking for Defense) line of effort, you will specifically own the end-to-end problem curation pipeline. In this role, you are responsible for guiding sourced military and government problems through the entire qualification and scoping lifecycle, ensuring they are perfectly refined and ready for distribution to university cohorts. You will manage the execution of key workflow tasks, enforce strict quality assurance, ensure clean CRM tracking, and guarantee that the final outputs meet the standards required for the H4D program and our Department of War (DoW) client.

Location: This is a hybrid position within commuting distance to our Arlington, VA office with the expectation of being in the office three days per week and sometimes more often based on customer needs. Occasional travel required within the DC metro area, around the US and internationally.

What You Will Be Doing (Responsibilities):

  • Pipeline Management & Execution: Own the core workflow of the H4D problem pipeline, driving sourced problems smoothly from initial collection through final scoping and formal approval.
  • Team Supervision & Task Delegation: Manage the workload and delegate tasks across the program analyst team to ensure that problem scoping and curation are completed in a timely, thorough manner.
  • Quality Assurance (QA): Provide meticulous review of the team's work to ensure problem formatting, linguistic clarity, structural narrative, and associated data elements are correct and highly polished before sending finalized problems to the PM.
  • Data Integrity & Salesforce Management: Supervise and ensure that all curated problem documentation, stakeholder details, and workflow milestones are inputted into Salesforce accurately and maintained cleanly.
  • University Distribution Readiness: Maintain ultimate responsibility for the overall quality of the curated problem portfolio, verifying that problems are technically viable, operationally compelling, and fully actionable for university students.
  • Mentorship & Guidance: Provide active mentorship, structural support, and constructive feedback on job performance to analysts, ensuring long-term continuous improvement and alignment over time.
  • Stakeholder Coordination: Serve as a reliable touchpoint for project communications, leading meetings/calls with customers or problem sponsors, and managing scheduling requirements for industry or government engagements.
  • Methodology Alignment: Maintain a deep and rich understanding of BMNT products, services, and core methodologies (Lean Startup, H4X, Design Thinking), articulating how these address customer needs and recommending pipeline updates when necessary.
  • BMNT Culture: Model the desired behaviors of a successful contributor at BMNT and fully embrace the BMNT Bushido.

Experience and Qualifications You’ll Need to Thrive in this Role:

  • Education & Experience: Bachelor's Degree or equivalent work experience. Requires at least 6+ years of consulting or relevant project management experience.
  • Detail & Quality Focus: Meticulous attention to detail. Strong capability to evaluate datasets and written briefs to ensure absolute data validity, formatting accuracy, and structural integrity.
  • CRM/Database Competency: Experience with complex project pipelines; proficiency tracking and entering programmatic milestones within CRM systems (Salesforce strongly preferred).
  • Problem Solving & Analytics: Exceptional analytical skills with a genuine passion for deconstructing messy, complex, and intractable national security or organizational problems into curated, structured insights.
  • Innovation Methodologies: Familiarity with modern innovation methodologies (Lean Startup, DevOps, Design Thinking, Rapid Prototyping, Agile, etc.) and/or previous exposure to the Hacking for Defense (H4D) curriculum is highly preferred.
  • Subject Matter Acumen: Foundational subject matter expertise or rapid familiarity with government, military, or emerging defense technology sectors.
  • Communication Excellence: Superb verbal and written communication skills—specifically the ability to transform voluminous information into highly succinct, actionable insights with minimal correction required.
  • Professional Character: Exhibits high emotional intelligence (EQ) through active listening, welcoming performance feedback, demonstrating thoughtful judgment, humility, and self-awareness.

Additional Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizenship required.
  • Occasional travel required within the DC metro area, around the US and internationally.
  • Passion for BMNT’s mission and commitment to enabling innovation at scale within the federal enterprise.

If you are a self-starter with an obsession for outcomes, not activities and a history of achievements, and enjoy working on projects with collaborative and creative teams, this could be the right role for you!

title: Resin Technician - Night Shift
description:
The resin technician position is responsible for manufacturing resin (solvent acrylics and alkyds) and latex products. The total job is made up of four basic job components. The person must also participate individually and/or as a group in team settings, employee training, presentations and other activities that are essential to the attainment of the team, plant, and/or site goals.

Job duties include contact with other employees, operating heavy machinery, and access to proprietary information, raw materials, finished merchandise, and/or other items of value, and such access may be supervised or unsupervised. The Company therefore has determined that a review of criminal history is necessary to protect the business and its operations and reputation and is necessary to protect the safety of the Company’s staff, employees, and vendors.

  • Manually clean reactors and all component parts related to breakdown and assembly.

  • Remove hazardous waste from latex batches and dispose in proper drums.
  • Perform and participate in general housekeeping activities.
  • Perform all requirements pertaining to Batch Tracking functions.
  • Off-load and load tank wagons of bulk materials.
  • Participation towards completion of other related tasks and duties as directed or needed

Minimum Requirements:

  • Must be at least eighteen (18) years of age
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the country of employment without needing sponsorship for employment work visa status now or in the future

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Have prior work experience in the paint or chemical processing industry
  • Have familiarity with batch manufacturing processes
  • Have experience working with hazardous materials
  • Have at least an forklift certification or willingness to obtain certification
  • Have at least one (1) year of work experience using material handling equipment (for example: forklifts (stand and sit), pallet jacks, hand trucks, order pickers, vacu-hoists, drum dollys, conveyor belts, etc.)

  • Present clinical data and educational materials to physician sites and/or conferences within an assigned region or nationally, as required by Sales and Marketing.

  • Assists with other related duties and special projects as required by sales and marketing.

  • Function as a field trainer of assigned region to provide an extension of our Director of Training.

  • Regional speaking engagements (Roundtables, Grand Rounds, Tumor Boards, etc.) with physicians to broaden CMI understanding clinically.

  • Attend select regional tradeshows, national tradeshows and participate in sales meetings to present relevant data necessary to promote CMI and educate clients in the marketplace.

title: Ski Patrol Basic - Winter 26-27
location: Aspen or Snowmass Village, CO, us
description:
Patrolling at Aspen Snowmass is more than a job, it's an opportunity to build a career alongside some of the best Ski Patrollers in the industry. Operating across four unique mountains, our patrol manages some of the most iconic and challenging terrain in Colorado while delivering exceptional guest experiences and mountain safety. As a member of our close-knit team, you'll work alongside highly skilled professionals committed to excellence while continually developing your technical, avalanche, rescue, and leadership skills. Whether you're looking to advance your expertise or build a long-term career in ski patrol, Aspen Snowmass offers an unmatched opportunity to grow.

The Ski Patrol Basic plays an essential role in creating a safe, enjoyable, and memorable mountain experience for every guest. Working as part of a highly trained and collaborative team, this position responds to emergencies, promotes mountain safety, and helps maintain exceptional skiing and riding conditions through proactive risk management and guest service. Every day offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact while working in a dynamic alpine environment. This position reports to the Ski Patrol Director.

Job Posting Deadline: Applications for this position will be considered on a rolling basis until October 1, 2026.

Essential Job Functions / Key Job Responsibilities

  • Patrol assigned terrain to ensure a safe, welcoming, and high-quality mountain experience through proactive guest engagement, hazard awareness, and visibility across the mountain
  • Assess and manage daily mountain conditions, including trail status, signage, hazard marking, and coordination of trail openings and closures in partnership with mountain operations
  • Conduct end-of-day sweeps and closure procedures to ensure all guests have safely exited the mountain during normal operations and weather-related events
  • Respond to medical and emergency incidents by providing immediate care, coordinating transport of injured guests, and executing established emergency response protocols
  • Participate in lift evacuation operations, including training, preparedness, and execution under the direction of patrol leadership
  • Support snow safety operations, including avalanche mitigation activities, terrain evaluation, and rescue response in coordination with snow safety teams
  • Operate dispatch and communication systems with accuracy, clarity, and professionalism to support effective mountain-wide coordination and incident response
  • Perform snow surface management activities, including packing and improving snow conditions to support safe and consistent skiing and riding experiences
  • Other duties as assigned

Education & Experience Requirements

  • High school diploma or equivalent required
  • Current CPR certification required
  • Current Outdoor Emergency Care (OEC) or Colorado Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) certification required

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Working knowledge of ski resort operations, mountain safety practices, and guest service principles
  • Working knowledge of resort weather conditions, snow reports, terrain, base area facilities, and special events
  • Advanced skiing ability with the confidence to safely navigate all terrain and snow conditions while carrying patrol equipment
  • Strong verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally in emergency and operational situations
  • Ability to assess situations quickly, exercise sound judgment, and remain calm under pressure
  • Ability to provide compassionate, professional care while responding to medical emergencies and assisting injured guests
  • Ability to work collaboratively as part of a high performing team in a fast paced operational environment
  • Strong attention to detail to identify hazards and support a safe, exceptional guest experience
  • Ability to work outdoors in adverse weather conditions for extended periods of time while performing physically demanding work
  • Ability to maintain a professional demeanor and work a flexible schedule, including weekends, holidays, and extended hours as operational needs require

Work Environment & Physical Demands

  • Ability to reach, crouch, kneel, stand, bend or be on your feet for extended periods of time
  • Regularly work in wet, cold, hot conditions requiring the use of protective apparel/equipment to prevent exposure to the elements and may be required to walk on slippery and uneven surfaces
  • Must be able to frequently lift, push or pull up to 50 lbs. individually or with assistance

About Mortgage Solutions Financial

Mortgage Solutions Financial is a national mortgage lender headquartered in Colorado Springs, Colorado. We believe every client should be served with integrity, dignity, and respect. We are committed to providing mortgage solutions that support our clients’ best interests and empower them to make responsible, informed financial decisions.

About the Role

Mortgage Solutions Financial is seeking an experienced Mortgage Loan Processor II to support our Retail Processing team. This role serves as an important partner and liaison between borrowers, Loan Officers, underwriting, and third-party service providers throughout the mortgage loan process.

The Mortgage Loan Processor II is responsible for gathering and reviewing loan documentation, maintaining accurate loan records, communicating loan status updates, and helping ensure loans move efficiently from application through closing. What You’ll Do

  • Coordinate with appraisers, title companies, employers, and other third parties to clear loan conditions.
  • Communicate underwriting approvals, outstanding conditions, and loan status updates to Loan Officers and clients.
  • Prepare completed loan packages and submit them to Underwriting for approval.
  • Ensure closing instructions and required documents are delivered to the title company according to established deadlines.
  • Review final settlement statements with the Loan Officer before closing.
  • Collaborate with Mortgage Experts and internal partners to provide a smooth and positive client experience.
  • Maintain regular, reliable, and predictable attendance.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

What You’ll Bring

  • A strong understanding of mortgage compliance regulations, loan program guidelines, and loan structure.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Strong attention to detail, time-management, and organizational skills.
  • The ability to work independently while contributing effectively as part of a team.
  • The ability to succeed in a fast-paced, changing, and high-production environment.
  • A solutions-oriented approach and the ability to independently manage challenging situations.
  • A commitment to providing exceptional service to clients and referral partners.

title: Truck to Truck Technician
description:
Truck to Truck Technician Summary

The Truck to Truck Technician is responsible for safely moving, loading, unloading, palletizing, and transferring waste containers using a forklift. This position supports the efficient movement of materials between Company facilities, hubs, treatment plants, and direct generator locations while ensuring compliance with DOT, RCRA, environmental regulations, storage permits, and company safety standards. The Truck to Truck Technician also assists with transportation coordination, manifest tracking, and maintaining accurate operational records.

Schedule: There are three openings available. Two positions work 6:00 AM – 4:30 PM, and one position works 9:00 AM – 7:30 PM.

Pay range $21-23 an hour

Qualifications
  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • 0–3 years of experience in warehouse operations, logistics, material handling, or a related field preferred.
  • Forklift certification or forklift operating experience required.
  • DOT and RCRA training required.
  • OSHA 24-hour or 40-hour HAZWOPER certification with annual refresher training required.
  • Proficiency with Windows-based computer applications.
  • Strong organizational and multitasking skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to safely operate a forklift in an industrial environment.
  • Ability to meet the physical requirements of the position, including lifting, climbing, and material handling.
Responsibilities
  • Offload, palletize, stage, and reload waste materials using a forklift.
  • Coordinate loads between hubs, treatment facilities, and outbound destinations.
  • Ensure transportation activities are efficient and comply with storage permits and regulatory requirements.
  • Dispatch transportation from hub locations.
  • Assist with tracking hazardous waste manifest return timelines.
  • Maintain Hub Management databases and Outlook records.
  • Safely operate forklifts while following all Health & Safety policies and procedures.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and safe work area.
  • Perform additional duties as assigned to support business operations.

Clean Harbors has a commitment to excellence deeply rooted in a strong sense of tradition. Our entire business model revolves around keeping North American businesses green. We collect more than 200 million gallons of used motor oil each year and operate the largest re-refinery capacity in North America, allowing us to re-refine more than 150 million gallons annually.

Tonerne er Kildehusets basisgruppe og en del af et integreret dagtilbud med både vuggestue og børnehave. Vi arbejder tæt sammen på tværs af huset og er optaget af at skabe udviklingsmuligheder for alle børn. Lige nu arbejder vi med at videreudvikle vores struktur og læringsmiljøer – både ude og inde, så de i endnu højere grad understøtter det enkelte barns behov og deltagelse i fællesskaber.

Dine vigtigste opgaver er at skabe struktur, tryghed og udviklingsmuligheder for børn med særlige behov. Samtidig bliver du en vigtig del af det tværfaglige samarbejde omkring børnene og deres familier.

Du skal blandt andet:

  • planlægge og gennemføre pædagogiske aktiviteter med udgangspunkt i det enkelte barns ressourcer og udviklingsbehov
  • skabe en tryg, struktureret og genkendelig hverdag for børnene
  • understøtte børnenes kommunikation, trivsel og deltagelse i fællesskaber
  • dokumentere og følge op på den pædagogiske indsats
  • samarbejde tæt med forældre, kolleger og tværfaglige samarbejdspartnere
  • bidrage til den fortsatte udvikling af Tonernes pædagogiske praksis.

Hos os bliver du en del af et fagligt fællesskab, hvor vi hjælper hinanden og udvikler os sammen. Vi prioriterer sparring, refleksion og en åben dialog om vores pædagogiske arbejde.

Du får løbende faglig sparring fra eksterne samarbejdspartnere, og vores ledelse er tæt på hverdagen og prioriterer, at du få mulighed for at deltage i efteruddannelse, netværk og udviklingsforløb, som giver dig ny viden og nye redskaber i din pædagogiske praksis. Du bliver også en del af Klynge A, som består af 6 dagtilbud, hvor vi har et fælles fagligt, socialt og ikke mindst arbejdsmiljømæssigt fokus.

Vi er på udkig efter dig som er uddannet pædagog og har erfaring med – eller lyst til – at arbejde inden for specialområdet. Du trives i en hverdag, hvor struktur, relationer og faglig refleksion går hånd i hånd. Samtidig arbejder du tæt sammen med både kolleger og forældre om at skabe de bedste udviklingsmuligheder for børnene.

Vi lægger især vægt på, at du:

  • arbejder struktureret og skaber trygge, forudsigelige rammer
  • møder børnene med nærvær, nysgerrighed og faglighed
  • er nysgerrig på egen praksis og bidrager til fælles læring
  • ser forældrene som en vigtig del af barnets udvikling
  • har lyst til at bringe leg, sang, bevægelse og kreativitet aktivt i spil i hverdagen
  • Bidrager til et sundt og glædesfyldt arbejdsmiljø

Kom og besøg os

Det er svært at mærke en arbejdsplads gennem en jobannonce. Derfor vil vi meget gerne invitere dig forbi til en kop kaffe og en rundvisning. Så kan du møde os, opleve Tonerne og få en fornemmelse af, om det er her, du skal være vores nye kollega.

Har du spørgsmål, eller har du lyst til at komme på besøg, er du meget velkommen til at kontakte pædagogisk leder Sabrina Brichs på 21 13 47 93. Send gerne en sms, så ringer hun dig op.

Vi glæder os til at tage imod dig og få dig godt ombord både i opgaver og fællesskabet.

Kildehuset ligger på adressen Vejtoften 1, 2630 Taastrup, og bussen kører lige til døren, så det er nemt at komme til og fra arbejde.

Praktisk information

Stillingerne er på 37 timer om ugen med tiltrædelse 1. oktober 2026 med mulighed for tidligere start.

Ansøgningsfristen er 18. august 2026. Vi holder samtaler i uge 35.

Der vil være mulighed for at forhandle lønnen med udgangspunkt i erfaring og kompetencer, men den overenskomstmæssige startløn er 36.454,- kr. pr. md. plus pension.

Vi indhenter børne- og straffeattest samt referencer i forbindelse med ansættelsen.

Ansøgning, CV, uddannelsesbevis og anden relevant dokumentation sendes via kommunens rekrutteringssystem.

Vi glæder os til at høre fra dig.

title: CCTV Operator
description:
Job Title: CCTV Operator

Location: South India Zone – Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Kochi, Coimbatore, Visakhapatnam, Mysuru, Mangalore, Madurai, Vijayawada, etc. (Deployment based on client/site requirement)
Department: Security Operations / Technical Surveillance
Reports To: Control Room In-charge / Security Supervisor / Assignment Manager
Company: G4S Secure Solutions (India) Pvt. Ltd.

Position Summary:

The CCTV Operator is responsible for operating and monitoring surveillance systems to safeguard people, property, and infrastructure at client locations across South India. This role involves real-time monitoring, incident detection, reporting, and supporting emergency response through CCTV systems, access control integration, and event logging.

Key Responsibilities:

1. CCTV Surveillance Monitoring:

  • Monitor multiple live camera feeds in real-time from control rooms across various zones.
  • Ensure continuous surveillance of critical and sensitive zones such as entry/exit points, lobbies, warehouses, data centers, etc.
  • Immediately alert on-site security supervisors in case of suspicious activity, safety violations, or emergencies.

2. Incident Management:

  • Respond swiftly to unusual or abnormal activity, including intrusion, fire alarms, loitering, or unauthorized access.
  • Maintain video evidence and submit incident clips to relevant teams following chain-of-custody protocols.
  • Assist site teams during live incidents by guiding them using visual monitoring.

3. Access Control Support:

  • Monitor and verify access control events if CCTV is integrated with turnstiles, boom barriers, or biometric systems.
  • Cross-check identity and authorization of personnel or vehicles as per client SOPs.
  • Flag tailgating, force entries, or violation of visitor movement policy.

4. Video Archiving & Retrieval:

  • Ensure timely recording and safe storage of CCTV footage as per the site’s retention policy.
  • Retrieve historical footage upon request from the client or internal G4S supervisors.
  • Maintain accurate logbooks of footage access and storage transfers.

5. Equipment Maintenance Support:

  • Conduct regular checks on all CCTV equipment including cameras, DVR/NVRs, monitors, switches, and power backups.
  • Coordinate with the technical support team or client vendor for maintenance, servicing, or repairs.
  • Report any malfunctioning cameras or broken connections immediately.

6. Reporting & Documentation:

  • Maintain daily control room logs, shift handover notes, and incident records.
  • Submit daily/weekly security reports including observations, alerts raised, and footage reviewed.
  • Follow confidentiality protocols and restrict sharing of sensitive visual data.

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Education: Minimum 12th Pass. Diploma in Electronics, IT, or Computer Applications preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 1–3 years of experience in CCTV operation/control room roles
    • Experience in malls, tech parks, industrial plants, hospitals, or logistics hubs preferred
  • Age: 21–45 years
  • Language Proficiency: Working knowledge of English + regional language (Kannada, Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam) is mandatory based on location.
  • Typing & Computer Skills: Basic computer operation skills required (MS Word, Excel, CCTV software usage)

Key Skills & Competencies:

  • Alertness and high situational awareness
  • Familiarity with analog/IP cameras, DVRs/NVRs, VMS platforms
  • Calmness under pressure and strong incident judgment
  • Team coordination and communication
  • Ethical conduct, confidentiality, and integrity
  • Ability to work in 12-hour rotational shifts (day/night)

Work Conditions:

  • 8–12 hour shifts, rotating day/night schedules
  • Indoor, air-conditioned control room environment
  • Uniform and ID card will be issued as per client or site requirements
  • May be required to work on holidays/weekends depending on duty roster

Salary & Benefits:

  • Salary in line with Minimum Wages (Skilled category) for the state – Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala
  • ESI, PF, Bonus, Gratuity, and Leave benefits as per statutory compliance
  • Accommodation and food may be provided for remote locations or 24x7 duty sites
  • Night duty allowance applicable where relevant

Growth Opportunities within G4S:

CCTV Operator → Control Room In-Charge → Site Security Supervisor → Technical Security Supervisor → Operations Executive

description:

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Beginning Oct. 1, 2018, if you are not currently registered, the Securities Industry Essential (SIE) exam, FINRA Series 6/7, state registration (including 63 or 66 if required) and Life licenses are required - or must be successfully completed within 180 days of starting the role

Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act

This position is subject to the Dodd Frank/Truth in Lending Act qualification requirements for Loan Originators. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMC's review of your criminal conviction history, credit report, information available through NMLS, and any other information relevant to a determination by JPMC that you demonstrate financial responsibility, good character, and general fitness for the position. Note that any felony conviction within the last seven years will disqualify you from consideration for this position. Your continued employment in this position would be contingent upon compliance with Truth in Lending Act/Dodd Frank Loan Originator requirements.

In addition, this position requires National Mortgage Licensing System and Registry (NMLS) registration under the SAFE Act of 2008. As such, upon active employment with JPMorgan Chase, you will be required to either register on NMLS, or to update your existing registration as necessary to grant access to and reflect your employment with JPMorgan Chase. Your continued employment in this position with JPMorgan Chase is contingent upon compliance with the SAFE Act, including successful registration immediately after your start date, and timely completion of annual renewal and required updates thereafter.

Any information obtained during the registration, update, and renewal processes or through NMLS notifications may impact your employment with the firm. Any of the completed information you provide during the Chase on-line application process may be transferred, on your behalf, to NMLS by JPMorgan Chase. Please carefully review the information you provide to Chase for accuracy and consistency and with any current NMLS record, if applicable, before submitting. Further information about NMLS and registration requirements of registration can be found at: https://mortgage.nationwidelicensingsystem.org/Safe/SitePages/default.aspx

  • Use core Addepar systems like the Data Lakehouse to advise and strategize Ops and Data Governance infrastructure

PHISHING SCAM WARNING: Addepar is among several companies recently made aware of a phishing scam involving con artists posing as hiring managers recruiting via email, text and social media. title: Outpatient Clinical Nutrition Coordinator (Outpatient Oncology)-FS Clinical Nutrition-Mount Sinai Hospital-Full Time, Days
description:
Outpatient Clinical Nutrition Coordinator (Outpatient Oncology)-FS Clinical Nutrition-Mount Sinai Hospital-Full Time, Days

The Clinical Nutrition Coordinator provides quality nutrition care and education to patients and family members, under the direction of the Director of Clinical Nutrition. The Clinical Nutrition Coordinator coordinates departmental initiatives and education programs. Maintains level of clinical expertise for assigned area and recommends the appropriate nutrition therapy as it pertains to the patient's nutritional needs. Acts as a resource to all clinical staff and provides feedback for their professional development. S/he adheres to all applicable regulatory agency guidelines, and to department and hospital philosophies, standards, objectives and policies and procedures.

1. Demonstrates advanced practice in clinical focus area. Exhibits advanced knowledge and skills, seeking out professional development and educational opportunities to further expertise.
2. Evaluates the nutritional status of the patients by reviewing pertinent information obtained from the electronic medical record and the interdisciplinary healthcare team. Applies experience and knowledge of nutrition screening and assessment to provide medical nutrition therapy by developing and implementing individualized nutrition care plans for general and practice specific patient populations.
3. Provides individualized counseling to patients and caregivers, including management of food-drug interactions, therapeutic diets, and supplements.
4. Conducts nutrition-focused physical exams, as indicated, to determine risk and/or degree of malnutrition.
5. Documents all encounters in the electronic health record per Clinical Nutrition policy.
6. Completes necessary paperwork to support insurance billing/reimbursement process.
7. Completes and maintains administrative records, including productivity, annual competencies, and other documentation of direct and non-direct patient care functions, with timely submission to direct supervisor.
8. Functions as a vital part of the multidisciplinary team in designated practice, actively engages in discussions regarding the nutrition care of patients in the practice. Participates in interdisciplinary rounds and care plan meetings as needed.
9. Coordinates projects and activities, including nutrition related in-services, interdepartmental nutrition education programs, lectures, community-focused programs and external speaking events.
10. Assists with care of patients on home nutrition support. Evaluates nutrition support prescription and communicates with the clinical care team to ensure patients’ needs are met. Assists with discharge planning and hospital intake for patients on home nutrition support.
11. Demonstrates leadership through the coordination and implementation of initiatives that promote nutrition services in the practice.
12. Coordinates quality assurance monitoring and reporting activities. Demonstrates willingness to offer outcomes-based resolutions that promote sustainable improvement. Supports interdisciplinary performance improvement goals of ambulatory practice.
13. Develops and updates nutrition education materials that meet the specialized needs of the target patient population.
14. Precepts dietetic interns and instructs them on the competencies required to complete their assigned rotation, develops learning modules and completes student evaluations.
15. Participates in research activities for ambulatory practice.
16. Maintains a positive and professional demeanor and effectively communicates with patients, visitors, colleagues, hospital staff, and supervisors.
17. Accepts and incorporates feedback for clinical development.
18. Supports department/program goals. Adheres to department/hospital policies and procedures, quality standards and safety standards.
19. Performs other duties as assigned.

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited institution, with completion of ACEND (Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition & Dietetics)-accredited dietetic internship.
  • 3+ years of clinical experience
  • Registered dietitian (RD) from the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR) required
  • Certified Dietitian Nutritionist (CDN) from the NYS Department of Education Office of the Professions required or process initiated upon hire.
  • Advanced Certification, i.e. Certified Diabetes Educator (CDE), Certified Nutrition Support Clinician (CNSC), and/or Pediatric/Renal/Oncology Specialty encouraged, but not required

Compensation Statement

The Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS) provides salary ranges that comply with the New York City Law on Salary Transparency in Job Advertisements. The salary range for the role is $65,885.00 - $98,280.00 Annually. Actual salaries depend on a variety of factors, including experience, education, and operational need. The salary range or contractual rate listed does not include bonuses/incentive, differential pay or other forms of compensation or benefits.

title: ICB Program Manager, Executive Director
description:
The Program Manager will own end-to-end program management across Brazil-local initiatives supporting JPMorganChase’s investment in C6 Bank and ICB strategic initiatives in the UK and Germany. Job Responsibilities:

  • Provide structure and guidance to your projects and be a pragmatic voice of reason within the delivery to ensure focus on key priorities.

  • Build strong and collaborative relationships across different departments, including internal teams (e.g. product and engineering, compliance, operations and investments) and with our external partners.

  • Collaborate with your colleagues to define and continuously improve our project management tools and protocols.

  • Lead and coordinate from a program management perspective, Brazil-local initiatives related to JPMorganChase’s investment in C6 Bank, including delivery planning, co-operation initiatives, marketing initiatives, governance routines, and stakeholder alignment.

title: Immigrant Case Worker -  2025799
description:
Are you a person of compassion? An advocate for justice? Someone who stands up for the rights of the vulnerable and speaks out for the marginalized, the exploited and the forgotten? Do you believe in our calling as Christians to welcome the least of these and love our neighbor?

If you answered ‘yes’, to any of the above, World Relief, and millions of people around the world need you.

At this pivotal moment in time, we are rapidly expanding and growing our team to meet the increasing needs of our world. We are looking for people who want to use their gifts and talents to make a real and tangible difference in our world and the lives of the suffering.
If you’re looking for a purpose-driven career in which you can grow your talents, while also standing up for the rights of the vulnerable, we want you to join us today.
ORGANIZATION SUMMARY
World Relief is a global Christian humanitarian organization whose mission is to boldly engage the world’s greatest crises in partnership with the church. The organization was founded in the aftermath of World War II to respond to the urgent humanitarian needs of war-torn Europe. Since then, for 80 years, across 100 countries, World Relief has partnered with local churches and communities to build a world where families thrive and communities flourish.

Today, organizational programming focuses on humanitarian and disaster response, community strengthening and resilience, and refugee & immigrant services and advocacy.

POSITION SUMMARY:
This position has responsibility for providing case management to refugee and immigrant families, including providing ongoing cultural adjustment support, orientations, referrals, and mediation services. The Immigrant Case Worker will work closely with community organizations, churches, landlords, and service providers to promote successful community integration. This position is based in Chicago and may require visits to clients primarily in northern Chicago and the surrounding suburbs.

ROLE & RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Ensure provision of timely and appropriate services to newly arriving refugee families during their first 90 days post-arrival in accordance with program guidelines.
  • Service provision includes:
  • Ensure that clients promptly receive health screenings, enroll in public aid benefits, receive necessary documentation, secure internet access, obtain clothing & household items, and are enrolled in English classes
  • Conduct home visits and assessments with refugee families
  • Provide initial and on-going orientations to life in the United States as well as assist in creating an initial budget pre- and post-employment
  • Conduct additional screenings and follow-up evaluations for cases with minors traveling alone
  • Coordinate interdepartmentally on resettlement details including furniture provision, basic needs and grocery provisioning, utilities connections, airport reception, and transportation. · to legal services for adjustments of status, and referrals to various community resources.
  • Conduct comprehensive assessments with clients, develop individual service plans, and facilitate connections to appropriate services.
  • Ensure ongoing provision of timely and appropriate services to refugee and immigrant families to foster ongoing integration including referrals
  • Provide education/orientation to clients around budgeting, paying housing and utility bills, and connect clients to financial resources when appropriate.
  • Provide mediation services between clients and outside entities (i.e., neighbors, landlords, volunteers, service providers, etc.).
  • Coordinate interdepartmentally to provide wrap-around services.
  • Assist team in conducting workshops for educating clients and orienting them to life in the US.
  • Maintain timely and accurate client files, case notes, and reporting records.
  • Actively participate in department meetings, staff development opportunities, program trainings, community activities, and organizational events.
  • Provide supervision and accountability for department interns.
  • Collaborate with volunteers and Volunteer Services staff to support the work of volunteers engaging with clients to meet the goals of the client’s service plan.
  • Other duties as assigned

    • JOB REQUIREMENTS:

  • Mature and personal Christian faith
  • Committed to the mission, vision, and values of World Relief
  • Desire to serve and empower the Church to impact vulnerable communities
  • Able to affirm and/or acknowledge World Reliefs Core Beliefs, Statement of Faith, Christian Identity and National Association of Evangelicals' For the Health of The Nation document
  • Valid drivers license, access to reliable vehicle and ability to pass MVR standards
  • MS Office skills required
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule including occasional early mornings, evenings, and/or weekends

    • PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Highly self-motivated with strong follow-through and ability to work independently.
  • Adaptable and comfortable working in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to maintain detailed, accurate records
  • Strong mediation and problem-solving skills
  • Direct-service experience with immigrant populations preferred
  • Cross-cultural experience and/or knowledge of the refugee/immigrant experience
  • Excellent communication skills with people of varying English levels
  • Understanding of social service provision in Illinois and Chicago
  • Comfortable working in a team environment
  • Fluency in languages spoken by client populations preferred (Spanish, Rohingya, Burmese, Arabic, Dari, Pashto, Swahili, or French)
    • World Relief offers a competitive benefits package and employee discount program for full-time, Regular, employees.

title: Supervisor
description:
Job Description: Admin Support

Position Title: Admin Support
Employment Type: Full-Time, Permanent
Minimum Qualification: Graduate (mandatory)

Role Overview:

The Assignment Manager will be responsible for the end-to-end management of physical security operations across high-profile client sites in the South Zone of India. This includes ensuring effective deployment of personnel, compliance with client protocols, documentation accuracy, stakeholder engagement, crisis readiness, and operational audits. The Assignment Manager is expected to maintain high discipline standards, handle large-scale operations seamlessly, and serve as the bridge between the client, site security teams, and the G4S backend.

This role demands strong leadership, a proactive mindset, technical know-how, and non-negotiable communication excellence. Impeccable fluency in spoken English with the right accent, grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation is strictly mandatory.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Site Operations Oversight:

  • Plan and deploy daily security personnel as per shift schedules and site-specific SOPs.
  • Conduct briefing sessions across all shifts and ensure grooming, discipline, and attendance compliance.
  • Prepare and manage MDR, shift schedules, and site logs.
  • Carry out efficient patrolling of internal and perimeter areas.
  • Observe and respond to suspicious man/material movements.
  • Ensure access control compliance and critical access management (labs, restricted zones).
  • Maintain visitor/vendor records, key logs, badges, and lost & found registers.
  • Conduct weekly security training and refresher briefings.
  • Perform surprise night inspections to assess readiness of night staff.

2. Technical Systems & Documentation:

  • Ensure the uptime and functionality of CCTV, access control systems, and FAPA equipment.
  • Maintain workstations audit, badge audits, and access key audits.
  • Coordinate with facility teams for system rectification and AMC partner activities.
  • Take access approvals via eApproval portals.

3. Reporting & MIS:

  • Share daily, weekly, and monthly operations reports with G4S and designated site managers.
  • Maintain event trackers, alarms reports, RPM data, incident logs, and vendor performance records.
  • Support site managers in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Delhi, and Gurugram for consolidated reporting.

4. Emergency & Incident Management:

  • Act as the first escalation point for medical emergencies, duress alerts, or system-triggered alarms.
  • Liaise with EMEIA SOC for remote access control and video retrieval.
  • Prepare incident reports, investigate breaches, and implement CAPAs.
  • Conduct mock drills, shutdown protocols, and risk preparedness activities.

5. Client & Stakeholder Coordination:

  • Respond to client queries and share required reports (daily/weekly/monthly) within agreed SLAs.
  • Attend virtual coordination meetings with client-side managers to sync activities Pan India.
  • Coordinate closely with facilities and places teams for smooth operations, approvals, and events.
  • Handle onboarding/offboarding of employees with badge issuance and access revocation.

6. G4S Internal Coordination:

  • Share weekly duty rosters, attendance, and nominal rolls with G4S backend.
  • Coordinate on salary concerns, health insurance issues, and uniform issuance.
  • Maintain leave records and escalate absenteeism trends.
  • Work with Key Account Managers to resolve operations-related escalations.

Candidate Profile:

Minimum Requirements:

  • Graduate in any discipline (mandatory)
  • Minimum 5–10 years of experience in security operations management
  • Experience handling multi-location operations preferred
  • Prior exposure to multinational corporate environments in IT sector shall be very advantageous for the candidate.

Essential Competencies:

  • Communication: Fluent spoken and written English (mandatory); clarity, grammar, and pronunciation will be tested.
  • Operational Skills: Security deployment, documentation, SOPs, reporting tools.
  • Technical Proficiency: Familiar with access control, surveillance systems, e-portals, and Microsoft Office.
  • Leadership & Ethics: High integrity, team management skills, crisis-handling experience.
  • Behavioral Traits: Attention to detail, time-sensitive decision-making, calm under pressure.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

  • 100% compliance in daily deployment & reporting
  • ≥95% uptime for security equipment and systems
  • ≤2 critical incidents per year (with timely CAPA)
  • SLA adherence for report submissions and audits
  • Staff discipline, grooming, and performance audit scores ≥90%

title: Spiritual Care Practitioner, Riverview (PR-CP29-014)
description:
About The Role:

With discernment, wisdom, compassion and a passion for the spiritual well-being of residents, families, employees and volunteers, the Spiritual Care Practitioner promotes high quality, multi-faith, spiritual care aligned with the mission vision and values of Bethany Care Society. The Spiritual Care practitioner is responsible and accountable for the provision of assessments and interventions directed at optimizing the spiritual care to residents, families, staff and volunteers of Bethany. The Spiritual Care Practitioner models and promotes respect for diversity, accepting all people from where and who they are in the provision of culturally appropriate spiritual care and support, provides and assists with appropriate spiritual and religious practices.

What You Will Do:

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 1. Resident Centered Care: Promotes spiritual well-being; plans and implements Spiritual Presence through Ministry. • Facilitate and coordinate pastoral care to meet the spiritual needs of residents in a multi-faith context • Conduct or delegate worship leadership including sacramental ministry • Conduct or delegate weekly bible study, or other faith and spiritual development programs • Facilitate opportunities for prayer, reflection, meditation and rituals for the celebration of festivals and holy days for all faiths represented and services that honor the individuals served (e.g. Time to Remember, Blessing of Hands, Christmas, Holy Week, etc.) • Conduct ongoing spiritual assessments with residents in a timely manner • Maintain visibility and ensure availability to talk to individuals and/or groups about spiritual concerns • Attend and participate in resident /family conferences and interdisciplinary meetings providing information from spiritual assessment • Use familiar and appropriate symbols, hymns and songs • Provide/facilitate client-centered compassion-based counselling and support for residents, families, employees and volunteers 2. Documentation: Accurately tracks information and creates reports relating to spiritual care initiatives. • Ensure daily/monthly statistical reporting on resident care including attendance and engagement in programing and spiritual care initiatives. • Provide on-going spiritual care documentation 3. Teamwork: Promote an interdisciplinary team environment, by fostering an understanding of the unique contributions of all team members. • Promote constructive, supportive relationships with the Interdisciplinary Team • Respond promptly to referrals • Role model and assist the Interdisciplinary Team to provide resident-focused services • Seek opportunities to convey the Mission, Vision and Values of BCS within denominational and inter-faith groups • Actively participate in the recruitment, development and appropriate use of spiritual care volunteers • Engage with external spiritual care providers including chaplains, faith community representatives • Initiate and implement partnerships with faith communities and other groups which foster the mission of Bethany • Be familiar with multi-faith resources • Participate in Spiritual Care Department meetings • Monitor, evaluate and continuously improve the quality of spiritual care services • Coordinate, select, orientate and evaluate other spiritual care service providers and volunteers for the sites • Participate in the education of employees and volunteers related to their roles and responsibilities in providing spiritual care • Educate employees, volunteers, residents and families about Spiritual Care and the role of the Spiritual Care Practitioner 4. Safety: Contributes to a safe environment for residents, the team and self by understanding and adhering to safety guidelines and practices at all times. 5. Leadership: Upholds and promotes the organizations values and philosophy related in particular to ethics, morality and integrity. Role models Bethany’s vision, mission, values and follows the Standards of Conduct. • Participate in management and interdisciplinary meetings • Support and participate in articulating and implementing goals and outcomes of Spiritual care for the organization • In collaboration with leaders, promote the integration of spiritual care into the culture of the organization • Support the mission, vision, values of Bethany and Spiritual Care Department • Participate in the business planning process to ensure implementation of Spiritual Care initiatives and priorities • Role model respect for diversity in the provision of culturally appropriate spiritual care What You Bring: QUALIFICATIONS 1. Education • Master’s degree from an accredited theological school plus clinical pastoral education (CPE) – completion of two advanced Units or equivalent combination of experience and education • Formal training in working with persons with dementia or Alzheimer’s is an asset 2. Experience • 5 years pastoral and administrative experience desired • Experience of work with seniors is an asset • Experience within a multi-faith environment is an asset 3. Professional registration • Ordination and/or official endorsement for Pastoral Ministry within a religious denomination • Active membership with CASC 4. Additional skills • a. Able to work effectively in a physically and mentally demanding environment. • b. Listening skills, basic counselling skills, group facilitation, multi-faith experience, and program development • c. Must demonstrate an acceptable level of reading, writing, and comprehension of English language skills • d. Excellent observation, communication and problem solving skills

title: ADA Mobility Assessment Evaluator
description:
Make a Difference

At MTM Transit, you’re not just part of a team—you’re at the heart of a movement to remove community barriers nationwide. We’re all about breaking the mold with bold ideas, open conversations, and a relentless focus on what matters most: you. Here, collaboration sparks breakthroughs, learning fuels growth, and every voice shapes our future. Together, we thrive, push our limits, and work as team to help you reach your full potential.

What will your job look like?

The Mobility Assessment Evaluator (MAE) is responsible for reviewing ADA paratransit application materials, supplemental intake and professional verification forms, conducting in-person interviews for applicants, and performing functional assessments with applicants to determine eligibility for ADA paratransit service. The Mobility Assessment Evaluator (MAE) is also responsible for maintaining accurate documentation, and providing final eligibility determinations to the Client.

This position is contingent upon award of RFP.

Location: MTA Assessments- Baltimore, MD

What you’ll do:

  • Determines final eligibility based upon the application, interview, functional assessment and any supplemental information
  • Conduct in-person interviews to assess mobility capabilities and review any supplemental information provided
  • Determine what functional assessments the applicant will be required to undergo
  • Provide written eligibility determination documentation to Client within ADA required and contracted time frame
  • Reads and interprets ADA paratransit applications, intake forms, and professional verification forms
  • Review interview results and application paperwork and follow up on assessments and professional verifications, as needed
  • Provide further written documentation to Client upon request
  • Assist the leadership team in identifying process improvement opportunities
  • Conduct functional physical and/or cognitive assessment with applicants that may include:
    • Physical Functional Assessment using an outdoor course
    • Physical Functional Assessment using an indoor course
    • FACTS
    • MMSE
  • Apply information obtained to determine applicant’s capability to independently ride fixed route transportation
  • Provide required forms to administrative personnel for data-entry and eligibility letter generation
  • Participate in staff meetings with leadership and/or Client
  • Participate in community outreach and education as needed
  • Participate in initial and on-going training as required by MTM and Client
  • Complete all necessary reports, paperwork and maintain on-going applicant tracking logs and reports for MTM and Client
  • Input all information into Client software (Trapeze) and other software as appropriate
  • Build rapport and communicate effectively with MTM and Client personnel to include administrators, management, support staff and applicant while providing high quality customer service
  • Participate in appeals process, upon request
  • Maintain a positive attitude when interacting with individuals, support Staff and caregivers
  • Work with management and the Client to follow through on service issues, troubleshooting problems, concerns, complaints and training
  • Must conform to MTM’s HIPAA standards

What you’ll need:

Experience, Education & Certifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in human and social services, rehabilitation, behavioral health services, or a healthcare-related field (may substitute high school diploma or equivalent plus two (2) years of eligibility assessment experience, and completion of a job-specific eligibility assessment training program).
  • 3+ years of professional experience working with individuals with disabilities
  • Experience and knowledge with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) regulations and sensitivity to issues relating to people with disabilities and older adults
  • Capability to perform all required assessments to determine eligibility
  • Experience conducting information-gathering relating to ADA Paratransit eligibility
  • Related experience with regard to the functional assessment of individuals with disabilities along with experience working with individuals with disabilities

Skills:

  • Solid interviewing, assessment and observational skills and demonstrated ability to work effectively with a diverse population
  • Ability to be trained in administering a standardized evaluation tool and be able to consistently administer and score such a tool according to established protocols
  • Ability to clearly communicate their findings and observations on the required database reports and notes, as well as in certification letters
  • Intermediate level of proficiency or above with Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel & PowerPoint)
  • Desire to learn additional programs
  • Excellent organizational and multi-tasking skills
  • Ability to work flexible hours
  • Familiarity with MS Office Suite.
  • Ability to adapt to a rapidly changing environment
  • Ability to work under limited supervision
  • Ability to make clear and factual observations
  • Additional language skills are preferred
  • Ability to maintain high level of confidentiality
  • Knowledge of the public transportation system & services
  • Knowledge of ADA complementary paratransit regulations, including, but not limited to, the regulatory definition of ADA paratransit eligibility
  • Ability to work well with the elderly and individuals with disabilities

Even better if you have...

  • Licensed PT/OT Therapist or certification in COTA, OT, or PT preferred.
  • Knowledge of Paratransit guidelines, preferred

What’s in it for you:

  • Health and Life Insurance Plans
  • Dental and Vision Plans
  • 401(k) with a company match
  • Paid Time Off and Holiday Pay
  • Maternity/Paternity Leave
  • Casual Dress Environment
  • Tuition Reimbursement
  • MTM Perks Discount Program
  • Leadership Mentoring Opportunities

Salary Max: $29/hour

El Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA) de las Naciones Unidas salva vidas en emergencias y cambia la vida de millones de personas alrededor del mundo. La misión del PMA es ayudar a alcanzar la meta del Hambre Cero para el año 2030. En El Salvador, se enfoca en hogares vulnerables a través de la protección social con amplio enfoque en nutrición, apoyo a pequeños productores en acceso a mercados, aumentar la resiliencia ante el cambio climático en poblaciones vulnerables y dar respuesta en situación de emergencias de lento y rápido desarrollo.

Contexto organizativo:

La posición tiene sede en la Oficina de País de El Salvador, reportando directamente al equipo del programa GastroLab. Como parte de la estrategia de empleabilidad impulsada por el Programa Mundial de Alimentos (PMA), se ha promovido la formación técnica y certificación de 846 jóvenes en distintas sedes vinculadas al sector gastronómico y turístico.

La persona en esta posición deberá desempeñar sus funciones con un alto nivel de organización, confidencialidad y atención al detalle, garantizando el adecuado manejo de la información personal de los participantes y el cumplimiento de los estándares establecidos para la gestión de perfiles laborales en la plataforma.

Garantizar el registro oportuno, completo y preciso de los perfiles de los jóvenes certificados a través del programa GastroLab en la plataforma Hiring Room, mediante la carga de hojas de vida, actualización y verificación de información

Experiencia

· Experiencia deseable en atención al cliente o seguimiento telefónico, con capacidad para realizar llamadas de verificación y actualización de información de beneficiarios o participantes.

· Habilidad para comunicarse de manera clara, cordial y respetuosa, tanto de forma oral como escrita.
